chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Hasan ibn al-Sarri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The Adhan is recited with slow, melodious chanting, and the Iqamah is recited with rapid, brisk recitation."

key_terms.الْأَذَانُ: The call to prayer, announced to inform the community of the prayer time.
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةُ: The second call to prayer, announced immediately before the prayer begins.
key_terms.تَرْتِيلٌ: Slow, measured, and melodious recitation with clear articulation.
key_terms.حَدْرٌ: Fast, brisk, and concise recitation without excessive prolongation.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in recitation style between the Adhan and the Iqamah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the liturgical etiquette of the call to prayer, distinguishing between the contemplative, melodious recitation of the Adhan and the urgent, brisk delivery of the Iqamah. This distinction reflects the practical need to transition the congregation from a state of preparation to immediate presence, a nuance preserved in Shia fiqh to maintain the spiritual gravity of the Adhan while ensuring punctuality for the prayer.
